newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch transport group sends damage team to Spain.
newsitem.headline: Dutch transport group sends damage team to Spain.

text.p: The Dutch Transport and Logistics Association(TLN) said it is sending a team to Spain to assess the amount of physical damage to vehicles and cargo incurred during the 13 day-old Spanish trucking blockade.
Two representatives from TLN and two from insurance companies will travel to Spain today, a TLN spokeswoman told Reuters.
They will go to the Dutch embassy in Madrid to discuss the damage claims to be put forward to the Spanish government.
Around 500 trucks usually travel to or through Spain a day from the Netherlands, said the spokeswoman.

Meanwhile, TLN is urging its members not to travel to Spain unless it is absolutely necessary, she said. The spokeswoman said that if journeys cannot be avoided the truck drivers should use coast roads in Spain.
Around 100 Dutch truck drivers are in stranded in Spain, she added.
Yesterday an official representing Dutch transport associations said the strike was so far estimated to have cost the Dutch industry 10 million guilders.
Although "none of the drivers have been hurt, the atmosphere is very aggressive if the Dutch drivers do not follow the instructions" of the Spanish strikers, she said.
TLN, based near The Hague, represents 7,000 transport operators.
